title: No source fixes the cutover mechanics of RWB-DM-008: the extract dump, the pipeline step, the cutover record, the ten-day evidence and the DM007 instruction slice
source: Legacy story RWB-DM-008 (AC1, AC3, endpoints, screen and states); FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2, A2.11 and A2.13; TSD P1 v3 T3.2, T3.6 and T3.7; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 32 and 44
section: s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow; s11 Data; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13 Solution plan
description: AC3 is the whole of the owned criterion and it names only an outcome: ten clean days, a sign-off, read-only legacy tables and records served from the new schema. No source gives the shape of any of the four inputs the story must build against: the legacy Workbench cutover dump (layout, file name, read identity, one-pass rule), the release-pipeline step that runs the cutover as one-off bulk work and the record it keeps, the rule that turns reconciliation_result rows into a clean-day count with its reset, and the split of partner_instruction between RWB-DM-008 and RWB-DM-007, which name the same entity and the same field range so the handover cannot be idempotent until it is ruled. The legacy endpoints row says only that the migration is a cutover step run by the recovery service identity and that its breaks are listed on the reconciliation extract, so no operation, payload or record format can be fixed from it.
evidence: RWB-DM-008 AC1 and AC3; RWB-DM-008 endpoints row 'No endpoint in this story'; FSD P1 v3 A2.11.2 step 2 gives REC-01, REC-02 and REC-05 but no cutover path; TSD P1 v3 T3.2 gives the two-migration rule only; Architecture v5 slide 32 gives 'One-off bulk work' and 'Airflow never reads or writes rwb_* schemas' with no record shape; slide 44 gives JOB-04 Reconciliation with no clean-day rule; legacy RWB-DM-007 names partner_instruction as well and no ruling on the overlap exists.
proposed: Agree the cutover record, the dump interface, the clean-day rule and the DM007 instruction slice at the cutover rehearsal, record them in the runbook entry of the release pipeline and the description of the Flyway version, and keep the values in the values file rather than in code.

title: The DP08 catalog row and the Ownership Map disagree on which service owns the partner tables of RWB-DM-008
source: FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 (DP08 row: partner, partner_instruction, system of record Workbench, refresh ON_CHANGE); Ownership Map v1 (P1 rwb-source-data tables; partner, partner_user and partner_instruction with S9 rwb-partner); TSD P1 v3 T3.6 (the 13 P1 Workbench tables) and T3.7; legacy story RWB-DM-008 data row
section: s8 Business rules; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; s13 Solution plan
description: The FSD lists partner and partner_instruction as the Workbench tables behind data product DP08, which is a P1 data product, and P1 owns the catalog entry that names them; the Ownership Map gives partner, partner_user and partner_instruction to S9 rwb-partner in schema rwb_partner, and TSD P1 v3 T3.6 counts 13 P1 Workbench tables none of which is a partner table. The two readings produce two different stories: one in which P1 writes the partner rows in rwb_source_data, and one in which P1 extracts, hands over and writes no partner row at all. The legacy data row also omits fields behind 'and 1 more' and 'and 3 more' and names no field of partner_user beyond six, so the field list of the handover cannot be closed from the legacy story either. R3 precedence puts the Arch v5 catalogue above the FSD, so the Ownership Map reading is used, but the catalog text stays as published.
evidence: FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 DP08 row 'Partner performance | Workbench | None | partner, partner_instruction | ON_CHANGE'; Ownership Map v1 P1 table list has no partner table; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 counts 13 tables and excludes them; RWB-DM-008 data row 'partner: ... and 1 more', 'partner_instruction: ... and 3 more'; ASM-A6-tables-6 keeps partner_user with S9.
proposed: Restate the DP08 row of the data product catalog with rwb-partner as the owner of the three tables and a pointer to the S9 contract, and close the field list of the handover in the catalog definition of DP08.
